nodes.label: Two-Worker Split (§14, v4.11)
nodes.rationale: Isolates long-running LLM ingestion work from fast jobs (embeddings, cron). ARQ workers fail jobs whose function they do not have registered, so queue routing (_queue_name='ingestion') is part of the job contract, enforced by a static call-site scan test.

nodes.label: Startup Hook Chunk Recovery (ARQ Resumability)
nodes.rationale: ARQ does not natively resume partially-executed jobs. Resumability is application code: chunk_status checkpoints plus a load-bearing startup hook that resets processing->queued and extracting->extraction_queued. Without it, crashed in-flight chunks are silently skipped — a data loss scenario. As of v4.11 it runs on the ingestion worker only; running it on both workers would double-enqueue orphaned extraction jobs.

nodes.label: Triage/Extraction Human Review Gate (§11.5a, v4.6)
nodes.rationale: Cheap triage model runs speculatively on every chunk producing candidate estimates; the expensive extraction model runs only on human-approved estimates with precise intent. Operator corrects types, discards, and merges over-split estimates before extraction. Adds chunk statuses triage_complete and extraction_queued and the ingestion_triage_estimates table.

nodes.label: Pagination Convention — Page Envelope (§6, v4.11)
nodes.rationale: Page envelope {items, total, limit, offset}, limit default 20/max 100, ordering created_at desc with id desc tiebreaker so pages are stable under concurrent inserts. In-place /api/v1 shape change accepted as a pre-GA exception to the breaking-changes rule (no external consumers yet).

nodes.label: Iterative Ingestion as Primary Model
nodes.rationale: Single-pass processing of large documents produces unmanageable candidate review queues. Operator selects small batches (2-5 sections), controls review burden; partial completion is a valid state, not a failure. High-volume patterns are v1.1.

nodes.label: No Machine Can Confirm (§10.1)
nodes.rationale: Human confirmation of governed knowledge is non-negotiable. Enforced at the confirm endpoints (agent: role prefix -> HTTP 403), not at the credential layer. Workers may write to confirmed records (e.g. embedding vectors) but cannot perform the submitted->confirmed transition.

nodes.label: Embedding Lifecycle (§12.1)
nodes.rationale: Confirmation must be instant; embeddings catch up asynchronously via ARQ on every confirmed version. Graceful degradation: records without embeddings remain discoverable via tsvector full-text search; semantic_available flag signals coverage. Changing embedding models is a breaking operation (pgvector dimension fixed at schema creation).

nodes.label: PDF Ingestion (§11.9)
nodes.rationale: PyMuPDF hybrid outline+heading chunking handles three real-world failure modes (outline but no headings, headings but no outline, neither -> character-count fallback). Scanned-PDF heuristic: empty text extraction across the whole document rejects the upload; OCR out of scope for v1. SHA-256 duplicate detection on file bytes.

nodes.label: HTML Ingestion and Nav Discovery (§11.10, §11.11)
nodes.rationale: Playwright/Chromium headless rendering handles static and JS-rendered pages. Two modes: single page (heading-based chunking) and site-nav crawl (nav link discovery -> operator page selection -> per-page rendering). robots.txt compliance configurable via ingestion_html_respect_robots_txt. Auth-walled content deferred to v1.1.

nodes.label: JSON Ingestion (§11.12)
nodes.rationale: JSON bypasses chunking and LLM extraction entirely — the payload is already structured and LLM stages would discard information. Validated payload converts directly to ingestion_candidates; no chunks created.

nodes.label: Prompt Contracts (§11.16)
nodes.rationale: Prompts are code, not configuration: versioned markdown files under prompts/ingestion/ (triage, extract_task, extract_principle), loaded at startup, git history as version log. Strict JSON output schema, embedded known-good example, explicit invent-prohibition. Operator-editable prompts deferred to v1.1; read-only Admin UI display is a non-negotiable transparency requirement.

nodes.label: LLM Provider Strategy (§11.1, §11.2)
nodes.rationale: Any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions provider; per-pipeline base_url/model/api_key/timeout in system_settings with convenience-mode fallback to shared llm_base_url. Keys stored encrypted, never logged, never returned via API. Anthropic native supported via translation adapter.

nodes.label: Review Queue Claiming Model (§8.2)
nodes.rationale: Claiming, not assigning: self-organising review queue with no bottlenecks. Claims auto-expire after a configurable window (default 48h) via the ARQ cron so abandoned reviews return to the queue; former claimer is notified.

nodes.label: Ingestion Pipeline (§11)
nodes.rationale: Seven stages: structural decomposition -> section selection -> triage -> estimate review -> extraction -> candidate review -> commit. Three sources (PDF, HTML, JSON) converge on the same ingestion_chunks representation. Produces task and principle candidates only — workflow composition is always a human act; that judgment cannot be extracted by an LLM.

nodes.label: Step Quality Linting (§9.10)
nodes.rationale: Non-blocking advisory warnings (abstract verbs, missing completion criterion, empty action list) computed on write/read, never stored, suppressed on confirmed records. Surfaces quality signals to the author before review without blocking submission.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting (§17.1, Sprint 11)
nodes.rationale: slowapi with Redis backend: 30/min on GET /search, 10/min on POST /ingestions. Auth-failure rate limiting (5 failures/min per IP) deferred — counting only failures requires custom Redis counter middleware.
